title: IBPS PO Mains — Mock Test 1
description: Full-length 100-question mock test simulating the latest SSC CGL Tier-1 pattern. Free-flow timing across all 4 sections in 60 minutes. Negative marking 0.5 marks per wrong answer. 2 marks per question (total 200 marks). Visual-reasoning questions (mirror, dice, paper-fold) are substituted with non-visual reasoning of similar difficulty since text-only generation cannot reliably render those visuals. Includes 5 recent Current-Affairs questions (2026 Q1) in the General Awareness section: T20 World Cup 2026, AI Impact Summit, Bhubaneswar 2028 Athletics, PMGSY-III extension, and FDI inflows. These slots are refreshed periodically; valid until 30 September 2026.

questions.stem: In a code, 'POWER' = 'QPXFS'. How is 'STRONG' coded?
questions.explanation: Each letter shifts +1: P→Q, O→P, W→X, E→F, R→S. Apply to STRONG: S→T, T→U, R→S, O→P, N→O, G→H ⟹ TUSPOH.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem: In a code, 'FRIEND' is written as 'IULHQG'. How is 'CANDLE' written in the same code?
questions.explanation: Each letter shifts +3: F→I, R→U, I→L, E→H, N→Q, D→G ⟹ IULHQG ✓. Apply to CANDLE: C→F, A→D, N→Q, D→G, L→O, E→H ⟹ FDQGOH.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem: If '425' means 'GO HOME NOW' and '524' means 'NOW GO HOME', what does '254' mean?
questions.explanation: From the two clues: digit-to-word mapping is consistent within each. Comparing 425 (GO HOME NOW) with 524 (NOW GO HOME): the order of the digits has changed in a known way. We deduce 4=GO, 2=HOME, 5=NOW. So 254 = HOME NOW GO.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem: Find the next term in the series: AZ, BY, CX, DW, ?
questions.explanation: First letters go A,B,C,D,E (forward); second letters go Z,Y,X,W,V (backward). Next: EV.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem: Pointing to a man, Sita said, 'His mother is the only daughter of my mother.' How is the man related to Sita?
questions.explanation: The only daughter of Sita's mother = Sita herself. So the man's mother is Sita. Therefore the man is Sita's son.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem: Riya walks 5 km north, then 3 km east, then 5 km south. How far is she from her starting point?
questions.explanation: North 5 + South 5 cancel. Net displacement is 3 km east. Distance = 3 km.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem: A man walks 8 km east, turns left and walks 6 km. What is the shortest distance from his starting point?
questions.explanation: Net east = 8, net north = 6. Distance = √(64+36) = √100 = 10 km.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem:
Statements: All birds are animals. All animals are creatures.
Conclusions:
I. All birds are creatures.
II. Some creatures are birds.
questions.explanation: All birds ⊂ animals ⊂ creatures ⟹ all birds are creatures (I follows). Birds exist and are creatures, so some creatures are birds (II follows).
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem:
Statements: Some pens are pencils. No pencil is an eraser.
Conclusions:
I. Some pens are not erasers.
II. No pen is an eraser.
questions.explanation: Some pens are pencils, no pencils are erasers ⟹ those pens are not erasers ⟹ I follows. But other pens (not pencils) might still be erasers, so II is too strong — DOES NOT FOLLOW.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem:
Statements: All cats are dogs. All dogs are wild.
Conclusions:
I. All cats are wild.
II. Some wild are cats.
questions.explanation: Cats ⊂ dogs ⊂ wild ⟹ all cats are wild (I). Cats are non-empty wild, so some wild are cats (II). Both follow.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem:
Statements: No teacher is a doctor. All doctors are educated.
Conclusions:
I. No teacher is educated.
II. Some educated are not teachers.
questions.explanation:
I. Doctors are educated and not teachers, but other educated people might be teachers — so 'no teacher is educated' is too strong. DOES NOT FOLLOW.
II. Doctors exist (assumed) and are educated and NOT teachers ⟹ some educated are not teachers. FOLLOWS.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem:
Statements: Some books are novels. All novels are stories.
Conclusions:
I. Some books are stories.
II. Some stories are books.
questions.explanation: Some books are novels (which are stories) ⟹ some books are stories (I). Conversely some stories are books (II). Both follow.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem:
Statements: All metals are conductors. No insulator is a conductor.
Conclusions:
I. No metal is an insulator.
II. All conductors are metals.
questions.explanation: Metals ⊂ conductors, conductors disjoint from insulators ⟹ metals disjoint from insulators ⟹ I follows. II is the converse-fallacy: some conductors might not be metals.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem:
Statements: All apples are fruits. Some fruits are tasty.
Conclusions:
I. All apples are tasty.
II. Some apples are tasty.
questions.explanation: Only SOME fruits are tasty — those tasty ones might not include any apples. So neither 'all apples are tasty' nor 'some apples are tasty' is guaranteed.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem:
Statements: A > B ≤ C; D ≥ A; E < B
Conclusions:
I. D > E
II. C > E
questions.explanation:
I. D ≥ A > B > E ⟹ D > E ✓.
II. C ≥ B > E ⟹ C > E ✓.
Both follow.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem: Five people — A, B, C, D, E — sit in a row facing North. C sits at the right end. A sits to the immediate left of E. B is between A and C, but not adjacent to E. Who sits at the left end?
questions.explanation: C at position 5 (right end). B between A and C but not adjacent to E. A immediately left of E, so they're consecutive. Place: positions 1-2-3-4-5. With A,E consecutive and A left of E: try A=2, E=3. B between A and C, not adjacent to E: B at 4. D at 1. So order: D, A, E, B, C. Left end = D.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem: Six friends sit around a circular table facing the centre. P is opposite Q. R is to the immediate right of P. S is to the immediate left of P. T sits next to Q. U occupies the remaining seat. Who sits opposite R?
questions.explanation: Place P at seat 1, Q at seat 4 (opposite). R is to immediate right of P → seat 6 (since right=clockwise from facing centre = decreasing seat index in our scheme; in this convention seat 6=immediate right of seat 1). S to immediate left of P → seat 2. T sits next to Q → T at seat 3 or 5. U occupies remaining. The seat opposite R(6) is seat 3. If T=3, then T is opposite R. If T=5, U=3, U opposite R. Pattern allows T at seat 3 (more natural ordering), so T is opposite R.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem: Five people — A, B, C, D, E — live on a 5-storey building (floor 1=ground, floor 5=top). A lives above C but below D. E lives on floor 2. B lives on the topmost floor. On which floor does C live?
questions.explanation: B=5 (top). E=2. A is above C but below D — so D > A > C. Remaining floors: {1, 3, 4} for A, C, D. D > A > C with all three from {1,3,4}: D=4, A=3, C=1. So C lives on floor 1.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem: Four friends — P, Q, R, S — were born in different months: January, March, July, October (one each). P was born before Q. S was born in March. R was born after Q. Who was born in July?
questions.explanation: S=March. P<Q<R in month order, and the three months left are {January, July, October}. The unique increasing assignment: P=January, Q=July, R=October. So Q was born in July.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem: How many triangles are formed by 5 non-collinear points (no 3 of which lie on a single line)?
questions.explanation: Number of triangles = number of ways to choose 3 points from 5 = C(5,3) = 10.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem: Which Article of the Indian Constitution provides for the Right to Constitutional Remedies, called the 'heart and soul' of the Constitution by Dr. B. R. Ambedkar?
questions.explanation: Article 32 guarantees the Right to Constitutional Remedies — Ambedkar called it the 'heart and soul of the Constitution'. It allows citizens to approach the Supreme Court directly for enforcement of fundamental rights.
questions.subject: GENERAL_AWARENESS

questions.stem: The Directive Principles of State Policy in the Indian Constitution were borrowed from the Constitution of which country?
questions.explanation: DPSP (Part IV, Articles 36–51) were inspired by the Irish Constitution of 1937, which itself drew from Spanish constitutional thought.
questions.subject: GENERAL_AWARENESS

questions.stem: Which constitutional amendment is known as the 'Mini-Constitution' due to the wide-ranging changes it introduced?
questions.explanation: The 42nd Amendment (1976), passed during the Emergency, made sweeping changes — adding 'Socialist', 'Secular' to the Preamble, introducing Fundamental Duties (Article 51A), and altering the balance of legislature, executive and judiciary. Hence dubbed the 'Mini-Constitution'.
questions.subject: GENERAL_AWARENESS

questions.stem: Under the Indian Constitution, the term of the Rajya Sabha (Council of States) member is:
questions.explanation: Rajya Sabha members serve a 6-year term. One-third of members retire every two years (Article 83(1)).
questions.subject: GENERAL_AWARENESS

questions.stem: Who appoints the Chief Justice of India?
questions.explanation: Under Article 124(2), the Chief Justice of India is appointed by the President. By convention (now codified in the Memorandum of Procedure), the senior-most judge of the Supreme Court is recommended.
questions.subject: GENERAL_AWARENESS

questions.stem: The Fundamental Duties were added to the Indian Constitution by which amendment?
questions.explanation: Fundamental Duties were inserted as Part IV-A (Article 51A) by the 42nd Amendment in 1976, on the recommendation of the Sardar Swaran Singh Committee.
questions.subject: GENERAL_AWARENESS

questions.stem: Which schedule of the Indian Constitution lists the official languages recognised by the Republic of India?
questions.explanation: The Eighth Schedule lists the languages recognised by the Constitution — currently 22 (originally 14, expanded by amendments).
questions.subject: GENERAL_AWARENESS

questions.stem: The concept of 'Single Citizenship' in the Indian Constitution was borrowed from:
questions.explanation: India adopted the concept of 'Single Citizenship' (one citizenship for both Union and States) from the British Constitution, unlike the USA's dual-citizenship model.
questions.subject: GENERAL_AWARENESS

questions.stem: Who was the founder of the Indian National Congress in 1885?
questions.explanation: A. O. Hume, a retired British civil servant, founded the Indian National Congress in 1885. The first session was held in Bombay with W. C. Bonnerjee as president.
questions.subject: GENERAL_AWARENESS

questions.stem: The Quit India Movement was launched by Mahatma Gandhi on which date?
questions.explanation: The Quit India Movement was launched on 8 August 1942 at the AICC session at Gowalia Tank Maidan, Bombay. Gandhi gave the famous 'Do or Die' call. Arrests began the next day, 9 August.
questions.subject: GENERAL_AWARENESS

questions.stem: Which of the following events occurred FIRST in chronological order?
questions.explanation: Champaran Satyagraha (1917) was Gandhi's first satyagraha in India. Jallianwala Bagh = 1919; Non-Cooperation = 1920; Salt March = 1930.
questions.subject: GENERAL_AWARENESS

questions.stem: The famous Bronze 'Dancing Girl' figurine, dated to the Indus Valley Civilization, was discovered at:
questions.explanation: The Bronze Dancing Girl, one of the most famous artefacts of the Indus Valley Civilization (c. 2500 BCE), was unearthed at Mohenjo-daro in 1926 by Ernest Mackay.
questions.subject: GENERAL_AWARENESS

questions.stem: The Battle of Tarain (Second), fought in 1192 CE, was won by:
questions.explanation: Muhammad Ghori defeated Prithviraj Chauhan at the Second Battle of Tarain (1192). This victory established Ghorid (and later Delhi Sultanate) rule in northern India.
questions.subject: GENERAL_AWARENESS

questions.stem: The Union Cabinet in March 2026 extended which rural-roads scheme to March 2028 with a revised outlay, covering consolidation of major rural links connecting habitations to schools, hospitals and Gramin Agricultural Markets?
questions.explanation: Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana — Phase III (PMGSY-III) was extended by the Union Cabinet to March 2028. The extension covers Through Routes and Major Rural Links connecting habitations to GrAMs (Gramin Agricultural Markets), higher secondary schools and hospitals.
questions.subject: GENERAL_AWARENESS

questions.stem: The 'Sundarbans' delta is formed by which two rivers?
questions.explanation: The Sundarbans is the world's largest mangrove delta, formed by the confluence of the Ganga, Brahmaputra and Meghna rivers in West Bengal and Bangladesh.
questions.subject: GENERAL_AWARENESS

questions.stem: Which Indian city has been selected to host the 2028 World Athletics Indoor Championships, making India the fourth Asian nation to host the event?
questions.explanation: India was awarded hosting rights for the 2028 World Athletics Indoor Championships in March 2026, with Bhubaneswar (Odisha) selected as the host city. India becomes the fourth Asian country to host this event.
questions.subject: GENERAL_AWARENESS

questions.stem: The AI Impact Summit, the first-ever global AI summit hosted in the Global South, was held in February 2026 in which Indian city?
questions.explanation: The AI Impact Summit was held in New Delhi from 16-20 February 2026, bringing together policymakers, researchers and industry leaders. It was the first-ever global AI summit hosted in the Global South.
questions.subject: GENERAL_AWARENESS

questions.stem: The SI unit of electric current is:
questions.explanation: Ampere (A) is the SI base unit of electric current, defined since 2019 by fixing the elementary charge e = 1.602176634×10⁻¹⁹ C.
questions.subject: GENERAL_AWARENESS

questions.stem: The deficiency of which vitamin causes the disease 'rickets' in children?
questions.explanation: Vitamin D deficiency causes rickets (softening and weakening of bones in children). It impairs calcium absorption needed for bone mineralisation.
questions.subject: GENERAL_AWARENESS

questions.stem: Which is the apex regulatory body for the securities market in India?
questions.explanation: SEBI (Securities and Exchange Board of India), established in 1988 and given statutory powers in 1992, regulates the securities market.
questions.subject: GENERAL_AWARENESS

questions.stem: Which of the following is the highest civilian award in India?
questions.explanation: The Bharat Ratna, instituted in 1954, is India's highest civilian award. It's followed by Padma Vibhushan, Padma Bhushan, and Padma Shri (in that order).
questions.subject: GENERAL_AWARENESS

questions.stem: India's Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) inflows in calendar year 2025 stood at approximately how many US dollars, marking a 13% rise over 2024?
questions.explanation: FDI inflows in 2025 stood at USD 81 billion, 13% higher than in 2024 — signalling continued investor confidence in the Indian economy. India's current account deficit in H1 2025-26 was 0.8% of GDP, lower than 1.3% the previous year.
questions.subject: GENERAL_AWARENESS

questions.stem: Which trophy is associated with the sport of football in India?
questions.explanation: The Durand Cup, first held in 1888, is Asia's oldest football tournament and is associated with Indian football.
questions.subject: GENERAL_AWARENESS

questions.stem: In cricket, an over consists of how many legitimate deliveries?
questions.explanation: An over in cricket consists of 6 legitimate deliveries (no wides or no-balls counted).
questions.subject: GENERAL_AWARENESS

questions.stem: India won the 2026 ICC Men's T20 World Cup by defeating which country in the final?
questions.explanation: India defeated New Zealand in the final of the 2026 ICC Men's T20 World Cup on 8 March 2026. This was India's second T20 World Cup title.
questions.subject: GENERAL_AWARENESS

questions.stem: A bag contains ₹1, ₹2, ₹5 coins in the ratio 4:3:2 worth ₹120 in total. Find the number of ₹1 coins.
questions.explanation: Counts: 4k, 3k, 2k. Total value = 1×4k + 2×3k + 5×2k = 20k = 120 ⟹ k=6. ₹1 coins = 4k = 24.

questions.explanation: Total man-days = 6 × 12 = 72. With 8 men: 72/8 = 9 days.

questions.stem: Two trains start at the same time from stations 240 km apart and travel toward each other at 50 km/h and 70 km/h. After how long do they meet?
questions.explanation: Relative speed = 50+70 = 120 km/h. Time = 240/120 = 2 hours.

questions.stem: The average of 7 numbers is 35. If one number 28 is excluded, what is the average of the remaining 6?
questions.explanation: Sum of 7 = 7×35 = 245. After removing 28: sum = 217. New average = 217/6 ≈ 36.17.

questions.stem: The average age of 30 students in a class is 14 years. If a teacher's age is included, the average becomes 15 years. Find the teacher's age.
questions.explanation: Sum of students = 30×14 = 420. With teacher: sum = 31×15 = 465. Teacher's age = 465 − 420 = 45.

questions.stem: A shopkeeper marks an article ₹500 above its cost price and gives a discount of 20%. He still earns a profit of ₹100. Find the cost price.

questions.stem: If a shopkeeper sells two articles, one at a 20% gain and the other at a 20% loss, both at ₹240 each, what is his net profit/loss percent?
questions.explanation: When SP is same and gain% = loss%, there is always a NET LOSS of (gain%/10)² = (20/10)² = 4%.

questions.stem: Find the volume of a cube whose total surface area is 96 cm².
questions.explanation: TSA of cube = 6a² = 96 ⟹ a² = 16 ⟹ a = 4 cm. Volume = a³ = 64 cm³.

questions.stem: What was the immediate trigger for the 1991 economic reforms?
questions.passage_context: The 1991 economic reforms in India represented a decisive break from decades of state-led development. Faced with a foreign-exchange crisis, the government dismantled industrial licensing, reduced trade barriers, and opened key sectors to foreign investment. Three decades later, the outcomes are mixed but instructive. India's growth rate climbed from the 'Hindu rate' of 3-4 per cent to consistently above 6 per cent for many years; poverty rates fell sharply; and a vibrant private sector emerged. Yet inequality widened in the same period, and rural distress did not always ease as policy-makers expected. Critics argue that the reforms favoured capital over labour, while supporters maintain that without liberalisation India would still be living with chronic shortages.
questions.explanation: The passage states 'Faced with a foreign-exchange crisis, the government dismantled...'

Find the part containing an error.

(A) The number of students / (B) attending the lecture / (C) were higher / (D) than expected.
questions.explanation: 'The number of...' takes a singular verb. So 'were higher' should be 'was higher'.
questions.subject: ENGLISH

questions.stem:
Find the part containing an error.

(A) Each of the boys / (B) have been given / (C) a separate task / (D) by the teacher.
questions.explanation: 'Each of...' takes a singular verb. So 'have been given' should be 'has been given'.
questions.subject: ENGLISH

questions.stem:
Choose the correct passive form of:

'They built this bridge in 1980.'
options: This bridge was built by them in 1980.
This bridge has been built in 1980.
This bridge had been built in 1980.
questions.explanation: Simple-past active 'They built X' becomes simple-past passive 'X was built by them'.
questions.subject: ENGLISH

questions.stem:
Choose the correct active form of:

'A new policy will be announced by the government tomorrow.'
options: The government announces a new policy tomorrow.
The government will announce a new policy tomorrow.
The government has announced a new policy tomorrow.
The government announced a new policy tomorrow.
questions.explanation: Future passive 'X will be announced by Y' becomes future active 'Y will announce X'.
questions.subject: ENGLISH

questions.stem:
Rearrange to form a meaningful paragraph and identify the FOURTH sentence in the rearranged order.

(A) The decision was taken after consultations with stakeholders.
(B) The new fee structure will take effect from the next academic year.
(C) Universities have announced a revision of fees for postgraduate programmes.
(D) Students with financial difficulties may apply for scholarships.
(E) The revision had become necessary due to rising operational costs.
questions.explanation: Logical order: C (announcement) → E (rationale) → A (process) → B (effective date) → D (mitigation). 4th = B.
questions.subject: ENGLISH

questions.stem:
Rearrange to form a meaningful paragraph and identify the FIRST sentence.

(A) These ecosystems support millions of livelihoods.
(B) India has one of the longest coastlines in Asia.
(C) However, climate change is now putting them at risk.
(D) Stretching nearly 7,500 km, it hosts diverse marine ecosystems.
(E) Government policies are evolving to address these vulnerabilities.
questions.explanation: Logical order: B (general intro) → D (extends with detail) → A (significance) → C (problem) → E (response). 1st = B.
questions.subject: ENGLISH

questions.stem: Convert to indirect speech: She said, 'I am writing a letter.'
options: She said that she is writing a letter.
She said that she was writing a letter.
She said that she has written a letter.
She said that she will write a letter.
questions.explanation: When the reporting verb is in past tense, present continuous in direct speech changes to past continuous in indirect: 'am writing' → 'was writing'.
questions.subject: ENGLISH

questions.stem:
Choose the option that best replaces the underlined portion.

If I _was_ you, I would accept the offer.
questions.explanation: In hypothetical/subjunctive constructions ('If I ___ you'), the correct form is 'were' (subjunctive mood), not 'was'.
